sanskrit: tam u̍ ṣṭuhi̱ yo a̱bhibhū̍tyojā va̱nvann avā̍taḥ puruhū̱ta indra̍ḥ | aṣā̍ḻham u̱graṁ saha̍mānam ā̱bhir gī̱rbhir va̍rdha vṛṣa̱bhaṁ ca̍rṣaṇī̱nām ||
english: Praise him — the much-invoked Indra, who wins with overwhelming might, unresisted; with these hymns magnify the unconquerable, the fierce one who endures, the bull of the human peoples.

sanskrit: sa yu̱dhmaḥ satvā̍ khaja̱kṛt sa̱madvā̍ tuvimra̱kṣo na̍danu̱mām̐ ṛ̍jī̱ṣī | bṛ̱hadre̍ṇu̱ś cyava̍no̱ mānu̍ṣīṇā̱m eka̍ḥ kṛṣṭī̱nām a̍bhavat sa̱hāvā̍ ||
english: He is the warrior, the champion, the maker of battle-tumult, the one who meets the foe head-on; the mightily protected, roaring with Soma-juice, raining down great dust — alone he became the overwhelming one of human races, of all peoples.

sanskrit: tvaṁ ha̱ nu tyad a̍damāyo̱ dasyū̱m̐r eka̍ḥ kṛ̱ṣṭīr a̍vano̱r āryā̍ya | asti̍ svi̱n nu vī̱rya1̱̍ṁ tat ta̍ indra̱ na svi̍d asti̱ tad ṛ̍tu̱thā vi vo̍caḥ ||
english: Thou, the untamed one, alone didst crush the Dasyus and protect the peoples for the Ārya; O Indra, is that heroic might truly in thee, or is it not? Declare it clearly at the right time.

sanskrit: sad id dhi te̍ tuvijā̱tasya̱ manye̱ saha̍ḥ sahiṣṭha tura̱tas tu̱rasya̍ | u̱gram u̱grasya̍ ta̱vasa̱s tavī̱yo 'ra̍dhrasya radhra̱turo̍ babhūva ||
english: Indeed, O most overpowering one, I hold that the might of thee, the mightily born, the swift of the swift, is real and lasting; more fierce than the fierce, more powerful than the powerful, thou who art inexhaustible hast become the conqueror of the withholding.

sanskrit: tan na̍ḥ pra̱tnaṁ sa̱khyam a̍stu yu̱ṣme i̱tthā vada̍dbhir va̱lam aṅgi̍robhiḥ | hann a̍cyutacyud dasme̱ṣaya̍ntam ṛ̱ṇoḥ puro̱ vi duro̍ asya̱ viśvā̍ḥ ||
english: Let that ancient friendship be ours with thee — as when speaking thus with the Aṅgirasas thou didst smash Vala; O shaker of the unshaken, O wonder-worker, thou who settest armies in motion, thou didst unlock all the doors of his fortress.

sanskrit: sa hi dhī̱bhir havyo̱ asty u̱gra ī̍śāna̱kṛn ma̍ha̱ti vṛ̍tra̱tūrye̍ | sa to̱kasā̍tā̱ tana̍ye̱ sa va̱jrī vi̍tanta̱sāyyo̍ abhavat sa̱matsu̍ ||
english: For he, the fierce one, is to be invoked through prayers, the one who wields lordship in the great overcoming of Vṛtra; he who wins offspring and progeny, he the bolt-wielder, became the one to be stretched forth wide in the battles.

sanskrit: sa ma̱jmanā̱ jani̍ma̱ mānu̍ṣāṇā̱m ama̍rtyena̱ nāmnāti̱ pra sa̍rsre | sa dyu̱mnena̱ sa śava̍so̱ta rā̱yā sa vī̱rye̍ṇa̱ nṛta̍ma̱ḥ samo̍kāḥ ||
english: By his greatness, by his immortal name, he has surpassed the births of men and flowed beyond them; by his splendour, by his strength, by his wealth, by his heroic might, the foremost of heroes has his dwelling together with them.

sanskrit: sa yo na mu̱he na mithū̱ jano̱ bhūt su̱mantu̍nāmā̱ cumu̍ri̱ṁ dhuni̍ṁ ca | vṛ̱ṇak pipru̱ṁ śamba̍ra̱ṁ śuṣṇa̱m indra̍ḥ pu̱rāṁ cyau̱tnāya̍ śa̱yathā̍ya̱ nū ci̍t ||
english: He who was never confused nor spoke falsely, well-remembered by name — he chose Cumuri and Dhuni as well; Indra has crushed Pipru, Śambara, and Śuṣṇa even now for the shaking and the laying low of their fortresses.

sanskrit: u̱dāva̍tā̱ tvakṣa̍sā̱ panya̍sā ca vṛtra̱hatyā̍ya̱ ratha̍m indra tiṣṭha | dhi̱ṣva vajra̱ṁ hasta̱ ā da̍kṣiṇa̱trābhi pra ma̍nda purudatra mā̱yāḥ ||
english: Mount thy chariot, O Indra, with its upward-flowing, vigorous, and admirable power for the slaying of Vṛtra; take the bolt into thy right hand; delight thyself and stride forward, O giver of many gifts, in thy powers.

sanskrit: a̱gnir na śuṣka̱ṁ vana̍m indra he̱tī rakṣo̱ ni dha̍kṣy a̱śani̱r na bhī̱mā | ga̱mbhī̱raya̍ ṛ̱ṣvayā̱ yo ru̱rojādhvā̍nayad duri̱tā da̱mbhaya̍c ca ||
english: Like fire burning a dry forest, O Indra, burn down the demon with thy weapon — like the terrible thunderbolt; he who shattered with deep and lofty force, who drove forth the path, and crushed all sin and evil.

sanskrit: ā sa̱hasra̍m pa̱thibhi̍r indra rā̱yā tuvi̍dyumna tuvi̱vāje̍bhir a̱rvāk | yā̱hi sū̍no sahaso̱ yasya̱ nū ci̱d ade̍va̱ īśe̍ puruhūta̱ yoto̍ḥ ||
english: Come hither, O Indra, with wealth along a thousand paths, O thou of great splendour, with thy many powerful prizes; O son of might, come, O much-invoked one — even now no godless one should have power over the fruits.

sanskrit: pra tu̍vidyu̱mnasya̱ sthavi̍rasya̱ ghṛṣve̍r di̱vo ra̍rapśe mahi̱mā pṛ̍thi̱vyāḥ | nāsya̱ śatru̱r na pra̍ti̱māna̍m asti̱ na pra̍ti̱ṣṭhiḥ pu̍rumā̱yasya̱ sahyo̍ḥ ||
english: The greatness of the great-splendoured, ancient, vigorous one has been spread through heaven and earth; he has no enemy, no match, no firm opposing stand — the mighty one whose power through many forms none can withstand.

sanskrit: pra tat te̍ a̱dyā kara̍ṇaṁ kṛ̱tam bhū̱t kutsa̱ṁ yad ā̱yum a̍tithi̱gvam a̍smai | pu̱rū sa̱hasrā̱ ni śi̍śā a̱bhi kṣām ut tūrva̍yāṇaṁ dhṛṣa̱tā ni̍netha ||
english: Let that thy deed be proclaimed today — what thou didst perform when thou gavest Kutsa, Āyu, and Atithigva to him; thou didst sharpen many thousands against the earth, and boldly thou didst lead Tūrvayāṇa to victory.

sanskrit: anu̱ tvāhi̍ghne̱ adha̍ deva de̱vā mada̱n viśve̍ ka̱vita̍maṁ kavī̱nām | karo̱ yatra̱ vari̍vo bādhi̱tāya̍ di̱ve janā̍ya ta̱nve̍ gṛṇā̱naḥ ||
english: After thee, O slayer of Ahi, O god, all the gods then exulted — the most poetic of poets; when thou didst make wide space for the afflicted, for the mortal people, for the body, while they praised thee.

sanskrit: anu̱ dyāvā̍pṛthi̱vī tat ta̱ ojo 'ma̍rtyā jihata indra de̱vāḥ | kṛ̱ṣvā kṛ̍tno̱ akṛ̍ta̱ṁ yat te̱ asty u̱kthaṁ navī̍yo janayasva ya̱jñaiḥ ||
english: Heaven and earth and the immortal gods, O Indra, opened wide to that thy might; thou who doest all, bring into being what of thine is undone — generate a newer hymn through the sacrifices.

sanskrit: ma̱hām̐ indro̍ nṛ̱vad ā ca̍rṣaṇi̱prā u̱ta dvi̱barhā̍ ami̱naḥ saho̍bhiḥ | a̱sma̱drya̍g vāvṛdhe vī̱ryā̍yo̱ruḥ pṛ̱thuḥ sukṛ̍taḥ ka̱rtṛbhi̍r bhūt ||
english: Great is Indra, hero-like, filling the peoples, moreover doubly strong, unassailable in his powers; toward us he has grown in heroic might — wide, broad, well-wrought; may he be so through the doers of good deeds.

sanskrit: indra̍m e̱va dhi̱ṣaṇā̍ sā̱taye̍ dhād bṛ̱hanta̍m ṛ̱ṣvam a̱jara̱ṁ yuvā̍nam | aṣā̍ḻhena̱ śava̍sā śūśu̱vāṁsa̍ṁ sa̱dyaś ci̱d yo vā̍vṛ̱dhe asā̍mi ||
english: The divine insight itself ordained Indra for the winning of prizes — the great, the lofty, the ageless, the youthful; him who has swelled with unconquerable might, who even straightway grows without limit.

sanskrit: pṛ̱thū ka̱rasnā̍ bahu̱lā gabha̍stī asma̱drya1̱̍k sam mi̍mīhi̱ śravā̍ṁsi | yū̱theva̍ pa̱śvaḥ pa̍śu̱pā damū̍nā a̱smām̐ i̍ndrā̱bhy ā va̍vṛtsvā̱jau ||
english: With broad, ample forearms and many rays, measure out our glories toward us; like a herdsman turning cattle into the fold at home, O Indra, turn us toward thee in the fray.

sanskrit: taṁ va̱ indra̍ṁ ca̱tina̍m asya śā̱kair i̱ha nū̱naṁ vā̍ja̱yanto̍ huvema | yathā̍ ci̱t pūrve̍ jari̱tāra̍ ā̱sur ane̍dyā anava̱dyā ari̍ṣṭāḥ ||
english: Him, that Indra, the clever one of this power — we call him here now, eager to win the prize; even as the former praisers received him, irreproachable, blameless, unscathed.

sanskrit: dhṛ̱tavra̍to dhana̱dāḥ soma̍vṛddha̱ḥ sa hi vā̱masya̱ vasu̍naḥ puru̱kṣuḥ | saṁ ja̍gmire pa̱thyā̱3̱̍ rāyo̍ asmin samu̱dre na sindha̍vo̱ yāda̍mānāḥ ||
english: He who holds his vow firm, who gives wealth, who is magnified by Soma — he is the great lord of pleasant and noble goods; the streams of riches have come together in him along the right path, like rivers flowing into the ocean.

sanskrit: śavi̍ṣṭhaṁ na̱ ā bha̍ra śūra̱ śava̱ oji̍ṣṭha̱m ojo̍ abhibhūta u̱gram | viśvā̍ dyu̱mnā vṛṣṇyā̱ mānu̍ṣāṇām a̱smabhya̍ṁ dā harivo māda̱yadhyai̍ ||
english: Bring to us the strongest might, O hero, the most powerful vigour, O thou who overcomest the fierce; give to us, O lord of bays, all the splendours and the bull-powers of humanity, for our exhilaration.

sanskrit: yas te̱ mada̍ḥ pṛtanā̱ṣāḻ amṛ̍dhra̱ indra̱ taṁ na̱ ā bha̍ra śūśu̱vāṁsa̍m | yena̍ to̱kasya̱ tana̍yasya sā̱tau ma̍ṁsī̱mahi̍ jigī̱vāṁsa̱s tvotā̍ḥ ||
english: That exhilaration of thine, O unconquerable battle-winner, O Indra — bring it to us welling up; by which, aided by thee, we may think ourselves victorious in the winning of offspring and progeny.

sanskrit: ā no̍ bhara̱ vṛṣa̍ṇa̱ṁ śuṣma̍m indra dhana̱spṛta̍ṁ śūśu̱vāṁsa̍ṁ su̱dakṣa̍m | yena̱ vaṁsā̍ma̱ pṛta̍nāsu̱ śatrū̱n tavo̱tibhi̍r u̱ta jā̱mīm̐r ajā̍mīn ||
english: Bring to us, O Indra, the bull-like vigour that touches wealth, that swells up, that is of keen discernment; by which, with thy aids, we may gain over the enemies in battles — both kinsmen and strangers alike.

sanskrit: ā te̱ śuṣmo̍ vṛṣa̱bha e̍tu pa̱ścād otta̱rād a̍dha̱rād ā pu̱rastā̍t | ā vi̱śvato̍ a̱bhi sam e̍tv a̱rvāṅ indra̍ dyu̱mnaṁ sva̍rvad dhehy a̱sme ||
english: Let thy vigour come, O bull, from behind, from above, from below, from in front; let it come together toward us from all sides — O Indra, place in us the splendour that contains the light of heaven.

sanskrit: nṛ̱vat ta̍ indra̱ nṛta̍mābhir ū̱tī va̍ṁsī̱mahi̍ vā̱maṁ śroma̍tebhiḥ | īkṣe̱ hi vasva̍ u̱bhaya̍sya rāja̱n dhā ratna̱m mahi̍ sthū̱ram bṛ̱hanta̍m ||
english: With heroic aids, with the most heroic, O Indra, may we win the pleasant prize through those who have great hearing; for thou art seen as the king of both kinds of wealth — bestow on us the great, solid, mighty treasure.

sanskrit: ma̱rutva̍ntaṁ vṛṣa̱bhaṁ vā̍vṛdhā̱nam aka̍vāriṁ di̱vyaṁ śā̱sam indra̍m | vi̱śvā̱sāha̱m ava̍se̱ nūta̍nāyo̱graṁ sa̍ho̱dām i̱ha taṁ hu̍vema ||
english: Him accompanied by the Maruts, the bull who has grown mighty, the unstinting one, the divine commander Indra — the conqueror of all, fierce, the giver of overwhelming might — we invoke here for our aid with a fresh hymn.

sanskrit: jana̍ṁ vajri̱n mahi̍ ci̱n manya̍mānam e̱bhyo nṛbhyo̍ randhayā̱ yeṣv asmi̍ | adhā̱ hi tvā̍ pṛthi̱vyāṁ śūra̍sātau̱ havā̍mahe̱ tana̍ye̱ goṣv a̱psu ||
english: O bolt-wielder, deliver to these heroes the folk that thinks itself ever so great and among whom I dwell; for thus we invoke thee, O hero, for the winning on earth — for offspring, for cattle, for the waters.

sanskrit: va̱yaṁ ta̍ e̱bhiḥ pu̍ruhūta sa̱khyaiḥ śatro̍ḥ-śatro̱r utta̍ra̱ it syā̍ma | ghnanto̍ vṛ̱trāṇy u̱bhayā̍ni śūra rā̱yā ma̍dema bṛha̱tā tvotā̍ḥ ||
english: We, with these friendships of thine, O much-invoked, may we be the higher over enemy after enemy; smiting both kinds of Vṛtras, O hero, aided by thee, may we rejoice with great wealth.
